comments.body:
## Implemented — consolidation + AC4 decision recorded

**AC4 decision: ACCEPT the raising posture of `_config_sources.repo_root`'s final
`Path.cwd()` fallback.** Rationale (unchanged from the 3198 analysis this ticket quotes): a
silently-wrong repo root is worse than a loud failure. Detached children no longer reach the
fallback — `rebar._proc.spawn_detached` anchors every detached rebar child to a durable cwd —
and long-lived IN-PROCESS work (daemon threads, a reconciler run "as a daemon from anywhere")
must either pass `explicit`, set `REBAR_ROOT`, or accept the loud failure. The decision is now
recorded in `repo_root`'s docstring (the location AC4 names), citing this ticket. No behavior
change.

**The consolidation, per the certified plan:**
* `rebar._proc.spawn_detached(module, func, arg, *, env, stderr)` — the ONE implementation:
  PYTHONPATH bootstrap, `-c` re-entry stub, platform detach flags (`_detach_kwargs` moved
  here), stdio discipline, durable cwd via `detached_child_cwd(arg)`. It RE-RAISES; env stays
  caller-supplied (helper layers PYTHONPATH onto a copy). `_proc` stays a stdlib-only leaf.
* The three sites collapsed onto it: `push.py` keeps its secret-stripped
  `project_child_env(relationship="unrelated")` + `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always` env and its
  `except OSError` + `%r` log; drain/sweep keep their store-scoped log sinks, canonical
  tracker arguments, and broad `except Exception` logs. Per-site `_detach_kwargs` deleted.
* Tests: new `tests/unit/test_spawn_detached.py` — a STATIC source scan pinning that the
  spawn signature (`DETACHED_PROCESS`/`CREATE_NO_WINDOW`, the `sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv…)`
  re-entry) appears only in `_proc.py`; a stdlib-only-leaf pin; construction/env-copy/re-raise
  unit tests; `test_windows_detach_kwargs` migrated from test_enrich_drain.py as planned. The
  two argv-pinning tests (drain 2006 / sweep vicuna) now patch `_proc`'s own `subprocess`,
  since that is where the one Popen lives. The end-to-end cwd contract tests
  (test_detached_child_cwd.py) pass unchanged — they patch the global `subprocess.Popen`,
  which still intercepts the helper.

Behavior-preserving throughout: no exception-surface change, no env change, no argv change
(the `-c` stub now spells `import m; m.f(sys.argv[1])` instead of `from p import m; …` —
same import, same call). `make lint` (incl. complexity ratchet), `make typecheck`, and the
affected test files (spawn_detached, detached_child_cwd, compact_trigger, enrich_drain,
enrich_queue, push_strict/parent_exit/child_env: 232 tests) all green. Proceeding to Gerrit.

comments.body:
Follow-up under this ticket: a FOURTH copy-paste site landed concurrently. While change 2020 (the three-site consolidation) was in review, change "Trigger snapshot GC from attested gate resolution" (a3da2f4cce) merged with its own `_detach_kwargs` + PYTHONPATH bootstrap + `-c` re-entry stub in `src/rebar/_snapshot/gc_trigger.py` — exactly the propagation-by-imitation mode this ticket exists to stop, and the completion verifier correctly refused the close: the AC static scan (`test_the_detached_spawn_signature_appears_only_in_proc`) FAILS on merged main because gc_trigger.py carries the signature tokens.

Remediation (grounded in AC1 "exactly one implementation exists" — this is completing the ticket's own criterion, not new scope):
- `spawn_detached` generalised from one child argument to `*args` (>= 1): the stub becomes `{module}.{func}(*sys.argv[1:n+1])` with the src slot after the args; argv layout for the existing three one-arg callers is byte-identical. cwd still anchors on the FIRST argument via `detached_child_cwd`. Zero args raises ValueError.
- `gc_trigger._spawn_detached_gc` now calls `spawn_detached("rebar._snapshot.gc_trigger", "run_detached", str(root), repo_root or "", env={**os.environ}, stderr=log_fh)`; its private `_detach_kwargs` and hand-rolled Popen are deleted. The never-raise posture (broad `except Exception` + warning log) stays at the site, per the helper's re-raise contract.
- The old stub's `sys.argv[2] or None` coercion moves into `run_detached` itself (`repo_root = repo_root or None`) — identical semantics for every existing caller (None→None, ""→None, non-empty unchanged).
- One deliberate anchor change: the gc child's cwd was `str(root)` (the store root); it is now `detached_child_cwd(str(root))` = the store root's PARENT after realpath — equally per-host, durable, and outside any worktree; the child takes `root`/`repo_root` explicitly so cwd is only an existence anchor. The gc argv test now patches `rebar._proc`'s `subprocess` (where the one Popen lives) and asserts the derived anchor.
- New tests: multi-arg argv layout + zero-arg refusal; the static scan now passes over all of `src/rebar` again.

Validation: test_spawn_detached, test_snapshot_gc_trigger, test_detached_child_cwd, test_compact_trigger, test_enrich_drain, test_enrich_queue, push suites — all green; `make lint` (incl. complexity ratchet) and `make typecheck` green.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

rebar has three detached-child spawn sites that are near-duplicates of one another:

- `src/rebar/_store/push.py` — the async branch of `push_tickets_branch`
- `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py` — `_spawn_detached_drain` (+ `_detach_kwargs`)
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py` — `_spawn_detached_sweep` (+ `_detach_kwargs`)

Each independently repeats: the `parents[2]` PYTHONPATH bootstrap so a bare-python child can
import rebar, the `-c` stub that re-inserts `src` and calls back into rebar, the platform
detach flags, the stdio discipline, and the never-raise wrapper. The duplication is not
accidental and it is documented in the code itself — `compact_trigger._detach_kwargs` says
"mirroring :func:`rebar.llm.enrich_drain._detach_kwargs`", `_spawn_detached_sweep` says
"Mirrors ``enrich_drain._spawn_detached_drain``", and `enrich_drain._spawn_detached_drain`
says "Mirrors push.py's PYTHONPATH bootstrap".

## Why this matters — a defect has already propagated along this seam

Bug `3198-438c-72a5-470f` was a missing `cwd=` on the detached `Popen`: the child inherited
the spawning command's working directory, and when that was a `make worktree` worktree since
removed, the child died at `os.getcwd()`. It was present at ALL THREE sites, and it got there
by deliberate imitation across three separate tickets:

- `57114212cf` (2026-06-12, pre-trailer) introduced the pattern in `push.py`;
- `c1de-d6a0-6cef-4135` copied it into the drain — its plan says outright "POSIX reuses
  push.py's approach (`start_new_session=True`, `close_fds=True`) + its PYTHONPATH bootstrap";
- `1fde-becd-942a-4351` copied it again into the compaction sweep.

One omission, replicated three times over two months, because "spawn a detached rebar child"
has no single implementation to get right once. The next property this pattern needs — a
signal handler, an env projection, a resource limit, an fd discipline — will propagate the
same way.

## Scope (to be confirmed by whoever claims this)
- A single `spawn_detached(...)` in `src/rebar/_proc.py` (already the documented single source
  of truth for logic shared between detached spawn sites, and already home to
  `reap_process_group` and `detached_child_cwd`; it is a deliberate stdlib-only leaf with no
  `rebar.*` imports, which must be preserved). It would own the PYTHONPATH bootstrap, the
  detach flags and the durable cwd, and it RE-RAISES on failure — the never-raise posture
  stays per-caller, because the three sites do not catch identically (push.py catches only
  `OSError`, logging `%r`; drain/sweep catch broad `Exception` with `exc_info=True`) and
  folding the catch into the helper would silently broaden push.py's exposure. Each caller
  keeps its existing `except` clause and its own log line, so the refactor changes no
  exception surface. Callers would supply the child
  entry point, their stderr sink, and their child ENV — env construction stays per-caller
  because it differs materially (push.py passes its secret-stripped
  `project_child_env(relationship="unrelated")` projection plus `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always`,
  the drain/sweep pass a plain `{**os.environ}`); the helper only layers the PYTHONPATH
  bootstrap onto whatever env the caller provides, so consolidation cannot drop
  push.py's secret-stripping.
- The three call sites above collapse onto it.
- Test consumers of the per-site helpers move with them: 
  `tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py::test_windows_detach_kwargs` (and any other direct
  caller of a per-site `_detach_kwargs`) is rewritten against `_proc`'s platform seam —
  `_proc` exposes the detach-kwargs construction testably so the Windows branch keeps its
  API-derisked assertion — since the per-site helpers no longer exist.
- Related open question, deliberately NOT changed while fixing 3198: should
  `_config_sources.repo_root`'s final `Path.cwd()` fallback DEGRADE rather than raise? It was
  left raising on purpose — a silently-wrong repo root is worse than a loud failure, and the
  three detached children no longer reach it now that they get an explicit cwd. But the
  exposure survives for long-lived IN-PROCESS work, which cannot be given its own cwd: daemon
  threads at `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:575`, `src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor.py:523`,
  `src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py:440`,
  `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_heartbeat.py:69`, and a reconciler that
  `src/rebar/config.py:516` says "can run as a daemon from anywhere". Decide that posture
  once, here, rather than per-site.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Exactly one implementation of "spawn a detached rebar child" exists; the three sites
      call it and none re-implements the bootstrap or the detach flags.
- [x] A STATIC test (source scan over `src/rebar`) enforces that the signature of a
      DETACHED-REBAR-CHILD spawn appears only in `_proc.py`: the Windows detach tokens
      (`DETACHED_PROCESS` / `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`) and the bare-python re-entry bootstrap
      (the `-c` stub doing `sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[...])` back into `rebar.*`).
      A fourth un-exercised copy-paste site then fails the test rather than slipping
      past a runtime-only assertion. The three NON-detached `start_new_session` spawn
      sites (`grounding/harness.py`, `adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py`,
      `adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` — process-group reaping, not rebar
      re-entry) are out of scope and must stay untouched.
- [x] `_proc.py` remains a stdlib-only leaf with no `rebar.*` imports.
- [x] A recorded decision (accept or change) on `repo_root`'s cwd fallback for long-lived
      in-process callers — recorded as a comment on this ticket AND in the docstring at
      `_config_sources.repo_root` (verified by inspecting that location); if the decision is
      'change', the degraded fallback is implemented.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and CI's pytest invocation are green.

## Provenance
Observed while fixing `3198-438c-72a5-470f`. The cwd omission itself is fixed at all three
sites; this is the structural reason it was three sites and not one.
compiled_state.title: consolidate the three detached-spawn sites behind one helper
